title: 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics
matchup: Hopfield and Hinton (2024 Nobel Prize in Physics) vs Amari (1972), Ivakhnenko and Lapa (1965) and others
question: Do the earlier works and citation records support Schmidhuber's claim that the 2024 Physics Nobel rewarded methods republished without credit?

usual_credit.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton "for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks". The Nobel Committee credits Hopfield with the associative memory network of 1982, whose energy function ties neural networks to models from statistical physics, and it credits Hinton with the Boltzmann machine, developed with Terrence Sejnowski and other coworkers in 1983 to 1985, and with the restricted Boltzmann machines and layer-by-layer pre-training that helped make deep networks trainable in the 2000s.

claim.summary: Schmidhuber argues that the prize rewards methods whose relevant predecessors were not cited. He compares Hopfield's 1982 equations with Amari's adaptive recurrent network of 1972, and the Boltzmann machine with the 1975 Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass. He also names the earlier multilayer learning of Ivakhnenko, Lapa and Amari when challenging accounts of hidden representations and deep learning. His report, A Nobel Prize for Plagiarism, allows that initial omissions may have been unintentional but argues that continuing to omit known predecessors changes the attribution issue. That allegation is his interpretation of the citation record, not an agreed fact about intent.

quotes.text: The #NobelPrizeinPhysics2024 for Hopfield & Hinton rewards plagiarism and incorrect attribution in computer science.
Instead they republished methodologies developed in Ukraine and Japan in the 1960s and 1970s, as well as other techniques, without citing the original inventors.
Even in their subsequent surveys and recent 2025 articles, they failed to acknowledge the original inventors.
The awardees have not tried to defend themselves. They can't - the facts are the facts.

response.summary: The Nobel Committee's background document cites Amari and Nakano (1972), describes the Boltzmann machine as a stochastic extension of Hopfield's model, and credits earlier gradient methods. Amari congratulated the laureates and later said an identical associative-memory model had appeared in Japan, while also crediting their rediscovery and development of the ideas. Historian Hansun Hsiung describes Japanese and North American groups as working independently. These sources support assessing the later contributions separately from priority alone, but neither the committee's document nor Amari's comments is a direct answer by Hopfield or Hinton to Schmidhuber's plagiarism allegation.

agreed_facts: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for Hopfield and Hinton on 8 October 2024.

Amari published a recurrent network of threshold elements that learns patterns in IEEE Transactions on Computers in 1972, ten years before Hopfield's 1982 paper in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The Nobel Committee's scientific background cites both Amari (1972) and Nakano (1972) among earlier models inspired by magnetic systems.
Schmidhuber and Amari both say that Hopfield's 1982 paper cites a later Amari paper on self-organization but not Amari's 1972 paper on associative memory.

The Committee's scientific background says that Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams reinvented a scheme for computing gradients that others had applied before, and it cites Werbos (1982) and Linnainmaa (1970) for that earlier use.
Schmidhuber published "A Nobel Prize for Plagiarism" on 7 December 2024 and issued revised versions on 31 July 2025 and 7 October 2025.
crux: The sources differ on whether Hopfield's network and the Boltzmann machine are the same methods as the earlier work (Amari's 1972 network, the Ivakhnenko and Amari learning procedures, the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model) or new contributions with those works as precursors. They also differ on whether failing to cite earlier work that the authors may not have known is plagiarism, as Schmidhuber argues, or independent rediscovery, as Amari's own comments suggest.

card.question: Did the 2024 Physics Nobel reward methods that others had published years earlier?
card.claim: He says the prize rewards methods republished from earlier Ukrainian and Japanese work, such as Amari's 1972 network, without citing the original inventors.
card.pushback: Amari says the laureates rediscovered and advanced the earlier ideas, and a historian says the North American and Japanese groups worked independently.
card.crux: The question is whether the laureates' methods match the earlier work, and whether leaving it uncited was plagiarism or independent rediscovery.
